description: Agent-run knowledge processing may improve vault quality while atrophying human understanding and knowledge-work skills.
topics: ["[[agent-cognition]]"]
source: TFT research corpus (00_inbox/heinrich/)

"To fully automate [metadata creation] is to outsource the very cognitive process that PKM seeks to enhance." Three risks: agents can hide the Collector's Fallacy behind an orderly vault; bypass the generation effect by doing the active transformation themselves; and decouple the human from the extended cognitive system. Industry “vibe notetaking” normalizes this delegation.

The counterargument is that humans retain judgment as curators. The open question: does approving agent work provide enough cognitive engagement to preserve the skills needed to do it independently? Unlike concern about remembering particular content, this concerns skill atrophy. A warning sign is being unable to imagine working without the agent.

Possible mitigations include deliberate manual processing and focused, smaller-scope review instead of blanket approval. The risk parallels invisible LLM attention degradation: output can look sound while underlying capability declines.
